title: CausalGeD: Blending Causality and Diffusion for Spatial Gene Expression Generation

problem.claim: Integrating scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data is important for understanding gene expression in spatial context.

gap.claim: Existing integration methods have limited performance, which the authors attribute to not considering causal relationships between genes.

contributions.claim: CausalGeD combines diffusion and autoregressive processes to leverage causal relationships between genes.
The model generalizes the Causal Attention Transformer from image generation to gene expression data and captures regulatory mechanisms without predefined relationships.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across 10 tissue datasets, CausalGeD outperformed state-of-the-art baselines by 5–32% on key metrics including Pearson's correlation and structural similarity.
The authors report that the method advances both technical and biological insights.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper motivates integrating scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics to understand gene expression in spatial context.
Existing integration methods show limited performance, attributed to ignoring causal gene relationships.
CausalGeD combines diffusion and autoregressive processes to use causal relationships.
The model adapts the Causal Attention Transformer to gene expression data to capture regulatory mechanisms without predefined relationships.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across 10 tissue datasets.

source_observation.claim: The authors attribute existing performance limitations to failure to consider causal relationships between genes.

interpretation.claim: For gene-expression integration, modeling relationships among variables may address limitations that remain when methods focus primarily on predictive generation.

application.claim: When designing spatial gene-expression generation systems, consider incorporating causal or regulatory structure into the modeling process.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond the 10 evaluated tissue datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the 10 tissue datasets.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols, baseline identities, or exact metric values.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results.
